declared_purpose: Manage user-selected files: organize by type/date, batch rename, detect and clean duplicate contents, and synchronize or back up directories (SKILL.md:2-3,10-63,88-112). Explicit safety requirements include preview unless --execute, yes confirmation, skipping symbolic links, and conflict protection (SKILL.md:114-119). Multiple backups, offsite storage, and scheduling are recommendations (references/best_practices.md:39-54,64-77). The package declares standard-library-only dependencies (requirements.txt:1-2). Size classification and bidirectional synchronization remain stubs (scripts/organize.py:199-204; scripts/sync.py:152-155).

data_operations.operation: Enumerate local files and infer organization categories
data_operations.data_scope: Recursive file paths and extensions; modification timestamps for date organization. Categories derive from extensions, and date folders derive from modification time, not file contents.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: In-process grouping dictionaries; stdout previews show category/date counts and up to five relative paths per type or three names per date.
data_operations.condition: Runs during previews and execution. Encountered symbolic-link entries and already categorized/date-folder files are skipped according to the selected strategy.

data_operations.operation: Persist organized copies or move originals
data_operations.data_scope: Eligible files and their contents; copy2 requests metadata-preserving copies. Folder names persist inferred type or modification-date categories.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Category/date subdirectories beneath the selected source directory. Copies retain originals; moves relocate them. Existing destination names receive numeric suffixes.
data_operations.condition: CLI requires --execute and yes confirmation. Copying is the implementation default; --move selects relocation. Direct helper calls use dry_run=False plus confirmation.

data_operations.operation: Select rename candidates, derive names, and return or preview a plan
data_operations.data_scope: Matching paths, names and extensions; requested prefix, suffix, regular-expression, sequence, case, and current-date transformations. No file-content read is implemented. Wildcard branches can include directories or symbolic links; the regular-expression branch filters with is_file but does not reject symbolic links.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Path-pair list returned to the immediate caller; CLI stdout receives old/new basenames, collision paths, and diagnostics.
data_operations.condition: Whenever rename planning runs, including without --execute. Selection uses --dir, defaulting to the current directory, and the supplied pattern.

data_operations.data_scope: Selected filesystem entries and their names; a selected directory rename also changes descendant path prefixes without reading descendant contents.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Computed destination paths, normally beside each original. Existing destinations are skipped. Results and errors go to stdout.
data_operations.condition: Requires --execute and yes confirmation unless --no-confirm is supplied. The confirmation bypass is an implementation option despite the entry document's unconditional confirmation principle.

data_operations.operation: Read candidate contents, infer duplicate groups, and report results
data_operations.source: scripts/deduplicate.py: find_duplicates, select_keep_file, and main; scripts/utils.py: calculate_hash
data_operations.data_scope: Recursive paths and sizes, complete contents of size-filtered files sharing a size, and modification times or path lengths for retention selection. The helper defaults to a 32-byte BLAKE2b digest. Reports include paths, sizes, keep/delete markers, totals, and a 16-character digest prefix.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: In-process size/digest maps and duplicate groups returned to the caller; CLI stdout receives the report. These operations establish no remote recipient.
data_operations.condition: Runs in scan-only and cleanup modes. Encountered symbolic-link entries are skipped; hashing excludes empty files and respects size limits. Files without successful hashes are omitted. Full candidate reads support content-based duplicate detection.

data_operations.data_scope: Recursive paths, file status, and sizes of zero-byte files; no content hashing.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Temporary empty_files list and stdout paths/counts.
data_operations.condition: Only with --include-empty. This separate traversal precedes ordinary duplicate detection; empty files do not enter automatic cleanup.

data_operations.data_scope: Group counts, duplicate counts, wasted-byte totals, full content digests as group keys, and stringified duplicate-file paths.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: The caller-selected --export filesystem path, opened in write mode; an existing report at that path is replaced.
data_operations.condition: Requires --scan-only, --export, and at least one duplicate group. Export is not performed on the cleanup branch or when no duplicates are found.

data_operations.operation: Delete duplicate entries or relocate them to quarantine
data_operations.data_scope: Every duplicate except the selected oldest, newest, or shortest-path representative.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: delete calls unlink on original entries; move relocates files into --to with collision suffixes. Paths and errors are printed to stdout.
data_operations.condition: Runs after yes confirmation when --scan-only is absent. delete is the default action; move requires --to. This CLI has no --execute gate, contrary to the entry document's general preview requirement. unlink does not establish secure erasure.

data_operations.operation: Create the synchronization target before preview or confirmation
data_operations.data_scope: Target directory names and any missing parent components; no file payload is copied by this operation.
data_operations.condition: Occurs whenever sync_mirror accepts an existing source, including dry-run and subsequently cancelled executions.

data_operations.operation: Inventory source and target, compare contents, and preview synchronization
data_operations.source: scripts/sync.py: should_exclude and sync_mirror; scripts/utils.py: calculate_hash
data_operations.data_scope: Recursive paths and file status on both sides; sizes of corresponding files; complete source and target contents when their sizes match. Inferred attributes are missing, changed, unchanged, or target-only status.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: In-process source_files, target_files, digest values, and action lists. Stdout shows source/target roots, up to 20 action paths, and totals.
data_operations.condition: Runs in mirror previews and execution. Encountered symbolic-link entries are skipped. Exclusions filter collected files but do not prune rglob traversal. Target-only inventory occurs even without --delete. Failed hashes cause the pair to be skipped.

data_operations.operation: Copy or replace synchronized files and optionally delete target-only entries
data_operations.source: scripts/sync.py: sync_mirror execution loop and CLI dispatch
data_operations.data_scope: Complete missing or changed source files, with metadata-preserving copy2 operations; target-only files selected for deletion.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Corresponding paths beneath the selected target. Updates replace existing target contents; deletion calls unlink. Names, errors, and statistics go to stdout.
data_operations.condition: CLI requires --mirror --execute and yes confirmation. Target-only deletion additionally requires --delete. Updates are part of the implemented sync path despite the entry document's general no-overwrite statement. Bidirectional mode performs no synchronization.

potential_excess.data_scope: An additional persistent copy of every file selected for organization, while the original remains.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Type/date subdirectories beneath the source, alongside retained originals elsewhere in that source.
potential_excess.condition: Organization executes without --move, where the requested outcome is one reorganized file set rather than a backup or retained source.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Classification requires organized placement, but retaining two copies is an implementation choice. Supporting guidance recommends a single data source while separately recommending backups.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Place each selected file in its required category/date location with collision protection.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use the existing move mode for organization requests that do not require source retention. This removes a redundant retained copy, rather than narrowing fields inside a necessary copy.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep copying available when backup, rollback, or original retention is explicitly required; preserve confirmation and collision handling.

potential_excess.data_scope: Content-derived digest prefixes added to duplicate previews.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: CLI stdout, received by the invoking terminal or agent.
potential_excess.condition: Every nonempty duplicate report, including scan-only previews.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The declared workflow requires a report and preview; it does not require exposing content fingerprints. Hashing internally is necessary for this implementation's detection method.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Show duplicate groups, identifiable file paths, sizes, and the proposed retained file.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use the existing group number without printing the digest prefix. This removes extra data from a required report.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain internal hashing; expose fingerprints when explicitly requested for verification. No onward disclosure from stdout is established.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full content digests persisted as duplicate-group identifiers.
potential_excess.condition: --scan-only --export with at least one duplicate group.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Exporting results is explicitly selected, but the full-digest schema is an implementation choice. File membership and counts can describe duplicate groups without retaining content fingerprints.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Persist group membership, identifiable paths, and requested scan statistics.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Replace digest keys with report-local group identifiers; offer full hashes as an explicit option. Preserve the report rather than removing the requested export.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain full digests if the user requires independently comparable fingerprints or a compatible hash-keyed format.

potential_excess.data_scope: Paths and file-status observations for unrelated target-only files.
potential_excess.condition: One-way synchronization without --delete still recursively inventories the whole target.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Source-to-target copying needs corresponding target entries. Target-only entries are used to construct deletion actions only when delete is enabled.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Determine existence, eligibility, size, and content equality of target paths corresponding to selected source files.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Without --delete, inspect only corresponding target paths instead of collecting unrelated target entries. This narrows a required comparison's read scope.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve exclusions, symbolic-link handling, copy/update decisions, and statistics; retain target-wide inventory for requested mirror deletion.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete contents of a corresponding target file after source hashing has already failed.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local hashing helper and synchronization process memory.
potential_excess.condition: Equal-size source/target pair where calculate_hash(src_file) returns None; target hashing still runs before the failure check.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Either hash failure makes the implementation skip the pair. The target digest cannot change that result after source hashing fails.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Mark the pair skipped when source hashing fails.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Check src_hash before calling calculate_hash on the target. This removes a redundant read; ordinary successful equal-size comparisons still require both hashes.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep the same skipped count and copy/update behavior; continue normal target hashing after successful source hashing.

potential_excess.data_scope: Persisted target directory names and missing parent directories during preview or cancellation.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: The selected synchronization target filesystem hierarchy.
potential_excess.condition: The target or parents are absent when sync_mirror runs, including without --execute.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The explicit workflow requires preview before execution. Creating an empty target hierarchy is unnecessary to calculate a preview.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Treat an absent target as empty when planning synchronization.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Defer directory creation until after dry-run handling and successful confirmation. This removes a premature persistence action, not file payload from synchronization.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Create required directories before approved copy/update operations and preserve previews for nonexistent targets.

potential_excess.data_scope: Symbolic-link entries and directories included among batch file-rename candidates.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Returned rename plans, stdout previews, and persistent filesystem renames when executed.
potential_excess.condition: A wildcard or fallback glob selects these entries, or the regular-expression branch accepts a symbolic link through is_file.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The declared operation is batch file renaming, with an explicit symbolic-link skip principle. Selection does not consistently enforce either boundary.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Apply a common symbolic-link rejection and regular-file filter to every selection branch before planning names.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve regular-file matching and naming transformations; support directory or link renaming only as a separately requested scope.

unknowns: Actual invocation arguments, selected files, sensitivity, and filesystem locations are unavailable. A selected destination could be local, mounted, or externally synchronized; source-level filesystem writes do not establish a remote recipient.
Caller handling and retention of normal function returns, stdout, errors, and confirmation input are unspecified. No onward disclosure or logging retention can be attributed from this package.
Root/ancestor symbolic-link handling, destination referents, and precise copy2 metadata or cross-filesystem move behavior depend on the runtime and filesystem; those implementations are not supplied.

The offsite backup recommendation identifies no service, recipient, transfer implementation, or retention policy (references/best_practices.md:41-54). Scheduling examples do not establish installed jobs; some sync examples omit the --mirror mode required by dispatch (references/best_practices.md:73-77; SKILL.md:88-92; scripts/sync.py:177-186).

Retention and later removal of organized copies, synchronized backups, quarantine files, and exported reports are unspecified. The supplied deletion paths establish unlink calls, not removal from snapshots, backups, or underlying storage.
